name: – Sophie Wilmès – Commission proposal to the Council
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council regulation on establishing the research and training programme of the European Atomic Energy Community for the period 2028-2032, complementing Horizon Europe, the Framework Programme for Research and Innovation, and providing for the Community’s contribution to the ITER project, and repealing Regulation (Euratom) 2025/1304
part_text:
1. This report sets out Parliament's opinion on a proposed five-year nuclear research programme for 2028–2032, worth about EUR 6.7 billion. Parliament wants more money for nuclear fission research, clearer budget lines so it can scrutinise spending, and a bigger push on small and advanced reactors, training nuclear workers, and replacing Russian nuclear fuel. It also wants Parliament consulted at every stage, though under the current treaty it only gives an opinion, not a co-decision.

- What changes: Parliament proposes amendments to the Council's draft, including a fixed split of the budget across ITER, fusion, fission and research.
- Who it affects: nuclear researchers, universities, start-ups, industry and the ITER fusion project.
- What happens next: the Council decides whether to accept Parliament's amendments or consult it again.
